metadata.name: Islamism
metadata.description: The Iranian Khomeinist constitutional variant: rule guided by a supreme jurist, Islamic limits on elected institutions, social obligations and national independence. This does not represent all Islamist movements or Muslims.
metadata.scope: Representative interpretation of Iran’s amended constitution and authoritative Article 44 economic policies, contextualised by Khomeini scholarship. Current UN reporting supplies explicitly distinguished implementation counterevidence; constitutional rights are not asserted to describe actual enforcement. This is one specified Islamist tradition.  Strict revision-2 re-audit: assess only source-supported positions on the exact questions. Unsupported empirical comparisons, modern technology analogies and institutional particulars remain unknown. Absence of doctrine is not a neutral position. This draft must not be used to calculate or publish a complete profile.
metadata.phrase: Islamic public authority, social responsibility and national independence, with electoral institutions operating within clerical constitutional supervision.

review.notes: Independent revision-2 review against all 240 exact questions, retained numeric claims and unresolved rows. Corrected institutional-premise substitutions and evidence overreach; source-supported nulls remain unresolved. This is a reviewed research draft, not approval to publish an incomplete placement. Question-level findings recorded in the audit report. 5 question corrections. Subsequent restored answers require fresh independent review; earlier peer review does not cover them. Restoration continuation: all 240 records compared with current wording and preceding independent review; 7 new research answers checked against primary passages. The collected addresses explicitly treat parental formation as causally important, including most corruption attributed to deprivation; qualified social-causal inference is defensible. Traditional gender/family transmission is directly prescribed. Moral disposition to immediate moral reaction remains interpretive, reflected by -1 rather than -2. No national-IQ or hereditary ranking is inferred. Dress rationale corrected to the specific 16 March 1981 fashion/dress passage. Incomplete evidence prevents publication; this review does not certify a complete profile.
